title: What is known about 1RB1LF_1LC1RB_1LF1LD_1LE0RD_1LB---_1LA0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_1LC1RB_1LF1LD_1LE0RD_1LB---_1LA0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. Seen in pairs of cells, each visit of the growing left end applies one recursive map to the tape; that map runs a counter in base 4 whose levels are long blocks of the word 111010. The counter itself can never halt; what the head does on the rare occasions it reaches the right end is not understood.
verdict: The question is open. The map from one wall visit to the next is known exactly as a recursion on words of pairs, with exact step counts, and the counter phases are proved in Lean. An accelerated simulator that finds its own rules, checked against direct simulation at every one of 1,425 wall visits (word and step number), runs through the seventh right-end event (wall visit 4.137·10148) to wall visit about 1025600 (step about 1.733·1051200) without a halt, and a level-stripping accelerator built on it shows that the next event cannot come before wall visit 108.73·10146. It is exact by construction but has not been re-derived independently. The right-end events do not stop, each one can in principle leave a halting word (such words exist, proved in Lean), and no invariant is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 56,686 cells have been visited and 39,117 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: A closed tape language from windows of 6 cells (closed: yes) covers the run; the only places it lets the halting transition E1 fire are E reading a 1 with the abstract left side in a window of 0s, followed by at least six 1s. With windows of 4 and 8 the same picture.

claims.title: An exact accelerated simulator
claims.text: py/blocksim.py keeps the tape as runs of 111010 and crosses each run with a shift rule; at every visit of the left wall up to 2·106 steps its tape equals the C simulator's (py/bscheck.py).

claims.title: The pair moves
claims.text: With X = 10, Y = 11, O = 00: F moving left swaps X and Y and turns round on a blank pair (reflect, flipX0/1, flipY0/1); Y B> X X becomes <F Y Y Y (turn0/1); Y B> X Yd X becomes X Od-1 Y Y Y B> (digit1, digit). For every count and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The first-block counter, phase by phase
claims.text: bounce, phase1, phase2, phase4_in, phase4_out: eight wall visits take 000 (1 0)n 0000000 R (digits) to 000 (1 0)n+2 0000000 R', for every n and every tape R, in 104n + 407 steps plus the time spent in R; R' is what one visit makes of R.

claims.title: A word of pairs that halts
claims.text: The wall visit of the tape X Y^7 X X halts after 253 steps. It is not a tape of the run from blank; it shows that the pair structure alone does not exclude a halt.

claims.title: The visit map is a recursion on words
claims.text: V(S) = G(S) with G(Y<sup>a</sup> X X U) = X<sup>a</sup> Y Y Y U, G(Y<sup>a</sup> X Y<sup>k</sup> X U) = X<sup>a</sup> Y G<sup>k</sup>(Y Y U), G(Y<sup>a</sup>) = X<sup>a</sup> Y Y: checked against the machine on 20,000 random words and on every covered wall visit of the run from blank tape (the recursion does not cover the right-end events).

claims.title: No halt in direct simulation
claims.text: A direct C simulator on blocks of 16 cells runs 10<sup>13</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt (the tape then reaches 300,908 blocks, about 4.8 million cells, to the left). The head reaches the right end of the tape at steps 1,937, 57,942, 61,755, 63,313, 83,647, 125,133, 48,737,226 and, after that, not again up to 10<sup>13</sup>.

claims.title: The recursion with step counts, checked against the machine
claims.text: On digit words: G(a T) = 0^a h(T) in 16 + 4a steps, h(0 T) = 3 + T, h(k T) = 1 + G^k(2 + T) in 2k steps plus the sub-visits, a unit 1 0 passes a hit in 26 steps. Fitted and then checked on 3,995 random words; the accelerated simulator built on it agrees with direct simulation, word and step number, at 1,425 wall visits (visits 1 to 1,422 (3·10<sup>6</sup> steps) and visits 112,522 to 112,524 (step 20,000,957,941)), with jumps of 1, 7, 50 and 1,000 visits.

claims.title: Accelerated run: no halt up to wall visit about 10<sup>25600</sup> (step about 1.733·10<sup>51200</sup>)
claims.text: The digit engine finds cycle, run and recursion rules by symbolic execution, and the macro simulator does the right-end events on cells. Rules added on 16 November 2026: frozen words emitted by cycle rules, and nested-frame rules for G<sup>12</sup>(2 (1 0 0 3 0)<sup>n</sup> X), which opens itself one level down. With them the run passes the seventh event (after wall visit 4.137·10<sup>148</sup>), where the old run stalled. The carries through the levels used memory quadratic in the depth, because each open level kept its own old copy of the rest of the word. Deep levels now drop their input and redo the call if the carry stops early, and each frame counts its steps locally. With that change the run reaches wall visit about 10<sup>25600</sup> (57,907 levels, descent 41,800 deep in 1.1 GB) with no further event and no halt. It was then stopped to free the core; the next jump would need about 4 GB. The run is exact by construction. It was validated against direct simulation (1,422 wall visits, words and step numbers, also with dropping forced on) and against the plain recursion on 400 random cases, but not re-derived independently.

claims.title: No right-end event before wall visit 10<sup>8.73·10<sup>146</sup></sup>
claims.text: At wall visit 10<sup>3200</sup> the word has 5,316 levels and then an eater on a fuel (1 0 0)<sup>m</sup>, m = 6.46·10<sup>147</sup>. With the fuel symbolic, 3,633 hits burn 27 units, pass 5 hits down and leave a block of four base-4 levels (×256); it runs K = 2.394·10<sup>146</sup> such rounds, which alone gives 256<sup>K</sup> wall visits. Then come descents: eaters of the ×64 kind on runs of a 20-digit rung, each fuel an affine function of the round count before it, shrinking by about 2.1 per phase. 42,000 phases in 233 descents, with no event, need 2<sup>2.899·10<sup>147</sup></sup> top hits. The bottom word does not run down (259 fuels (1 0 0)<sup>F</sup> before, 269 after): the fuels that start the descents shrink by the same factor of about 2.1 from one descent to the next, a hierarchy of the same shape at every level, so the event needs a rule for the levels. Checks: the phase jumps reproduce the twin's seventh event exactly and agree with plain batches on 6 words with a ×64 phase; the cached transitions between phases agree with the plain steps over the first 700 phases.

claims.title: The laws between phases, and a bottom word that grows
claims.text: Logged over 12,482 phases from the word at wall visit 10<sup>3200</sup>: after a ×64 phase (slack F − 4K of 5 to 9) the next fuel is fresh by law A, 11F′ = 21K + e with −913 ≤ e ≤ 224 (6,936 times), fresh by law B, F′ = K + δ with 2 ≤ δ ≤ 12 (1,401 times), or an older run of the word (4,063 times). The rung is a frozen word, so the hits a phase passes down cross every run of rungs. Below the eater the word is a list of staircases (runs a factor of 4 apart, about 210 each) between fuels (1 0 0)<sup>F</sup>, and the list grows: 362 runs longer than 1000 (25,957 digits) at the start, 1,164 (81,669) after 8,000 phases, 5,257 (322,122) after 12,000. The logged phases give the same bound as before (2<sup>2.899·10<sup>147</sup></sup> top hits), all of it from the first phases. Three fixes made the accelerator run past phase 30 again.
claims.where: 1RB1LF_1LC1RB_1LE1LD_1LB0RD_1LF---_1LA0LA/py/lsa_laws.py on the log of LSA_LOG=log lsa_run.py 2 3200, README

claims.title: The arithmetic of a descent
claims.text: For every value: under law A the fuel after j phases satisfies 21<sup>j</sup>(23F<sub>0</sub> + c) ≤ 44<sup>j</sup>(23F<sub>j</sub> + c) and 44<sup>j</sup>·23F<sub>j</sub> ≤ 21<sup>j</sup>·23F<sub>0</sub> + 44<sup>j</sup>·4hi, under law B the same with a factor of 4, and a stack of phases whose maps grow at least like a<sup>K<sub>j</sub></sup> needs at least a<sup>ΣK<sub>j</sub></sup> times the hits below it. The arithmetic only: that the machine's phases follow the laws is the log above.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The counter cannot halt; a right-end event could leave a halting word, and no rule for these events is known.

claims.title: The right-end events
claims.text: A right-end event is a hit that reaches the last digit of the word. Some are resets (the levels are crushed into single digits), some only turn the youngest ladder rungs back into fuel. They are simulated on cells; a rule for them on digits (a second recursion for the return sweep) is not known, and they keep happening: every event is a new chance for a halting word. The list of runs below the eater grows as the phases go on (see above), so the next event needs that list used up, and no rule for it is known.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.16×10<sup>18</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 2,166,473,947,245,007,495 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,010,334 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LA_1RC1RE_1RD0RD_1LA1RC_1RF0LE_1RA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Cut the tape into pairs of cells: every visit of the growing left end applies one recursive map to the tape, which builds a ladder of counters in base 4 and feeds it with fuel. A program that jumps over the regular parts has followed the machine to step 2.97·10<sup>297</sup> without a halt; the rare moments when the head reaches the other end of the tape keep coming and are not understood, and they decide the question.

facts.text: Pair moves and the four phases of the counter, proved in Lean for every tape.
A word of pairs on which a visit halts: the structure alone does not decide.
Wall visits before the next right-end event can come, so no halt before them (accelerated run, exact by construction, not a proof).

sections.heading: Pairs of cells: X = 10, Y = 11
html: Each time the head is in state F on a 0 with only 0s to its left (a wall visit) the tape to its right is a word of the pairs X = 10 and Y = 11. The wall is the growing end: it moves one pair to the left at every visit. The right end of the tape stays where it is for very long stretches.
From one wall visit to the next the word S becomes G(S):

G(Y^a X X U)     = X^a Y Y Y U                 turn back at the first double X
G(Y^a X Y^k X U) = X^a Y G^k(Y Y U)            a digit k: k visits of the rest
G(Y^a)           = X^a Y Y                     the blank right end, reached in B

What the head does: B runs right over the Y's. At a double X it turns back. At X Y^k X it erases the k Y's and refills two pairs, so k − 1 blank pairs stay behind it. On the way home F swaps X and Y in every pair, and a blank pair sends it right again: each blank pair is a small wall for the rest of the tape. These moves are proved in Lean (turn, digit, flip, reflect).

sections.heading: A counter in base 4, level after level
html: Write the word as digits (the number of Y's before each X). The six-cell word 111010 is the digit pair 1 0, and the tape is 000 (1 0)N1 w ... (1 0)N2 w ... (1 0)N3 w .... The digit word w behind a block goes through four phases:

One phase is two wall visits. The block gains one 1 0 in the second and in the fourth phase, and in the fourth the head goes on into the rest of the tape. For the first block all of this is a Lean theorem for every block length n and every tape R behind it: eight visits take 000 (1 0)n 0000000 R to 000 (1 0)n+2 0000000 R', and R' is exactly what one visit makes of R. So the rest of the tape lives the same life, eight visits to one: the second block grows four times more slowly than the first, the third sixteen times, and so on (5998, 1492, 372, 88, 21 copies after 109 steps).

sections.heading: When the head reaches the right end
html: When the last level overflows the head arrives at the blank right end in state D, and the recursion no longer applies. In the first 1013 steps this happened at steps 1,937, 57,942, 61,755, 63,313, 83,647, 125,133, 48,737,226. Some of these events only rewrite the last few digits; others are resets: a stretch of blank pairs is left inside the tape, a new counter starts to its right and uses the stretch as its wall, and the old blocks stay frozen until the stretch is used up.

The machine stops only when E reads a 1. The counter never brings that about, but some words of pairs do: on the tape X Y^7 X X a single wall visit halts after 253 steps (a Lean theorem; this tape does not occur in the run from blank). So whether the machine halts depends on the words that the right-end events leave behind, and nobody knows a rule for them.

sections.heading: Levels, fuel, an eater, and the rare events
html: Read the word right of the wall as digits: the lengths of the runs of Y between the X's. One wall visit then does this: G(a T) = 0^a h(T), where the hit h is h(0 T) = 3 + T (add 3 to the first digit) and h(k T) = 1 + G^k(2 + T) (the rest of the tape gets k visits of its own). Everything the machine does between two right-end events follows from these three lines, and the number of steps does too.
Four kinds of structure grow out of it:

• a level, (1 0)^n with a small digit word behind it that cycles through four shapes; four hits add two units and pass one hit on, so each level is four times slower than the one before;
  • fuel, a run (1 0 0)^m, made when an old level is taken apart;
  • an eater at the bottom of the ladder of levels, which burns three units of fuel every eleven hits and leaves new small levels behind;
  • a right-end event, when a hit gets through everything and reaches the last digit. Then the head runs to the blank end of the tape and comes back in a different way; some events crush every level into a single digit (a reset), others only turn the newest levels back into fuel.

A program that works on the digits, finds the repeating patterns by itself and jumps over them (it keeps the counts as big numbers) was checked against a plain simulation of the machine at 1,425 wall visits: the same tape and the same step number every time. It then runs on: through 4.137·10148 quiet wall visits, in which a ladder of 243 levels grows, up to the next event, at step 2.97·10297. No halt. There it meets a run of fuel too long for the patterns it knows, and stops.

The ladder can also be treated as arithmetic: each level is a counter digit with a known cycle, and an eater that burns its fuel a few units at a time builds the same block of levels again and again, so K of its rounds can be jumped at once with a geometric sum (proved in Lean for every K). At wall visit 103200 one eater has fuel for K = 2.4·10146 rounds, and every round makes the next one 256 times more expensive: the next event cannot come before wall visit 256K, a number with about 5.8·10146 digits. After that eater come long descents: eaters on fuels that shrink by a factor of about 2 each time, down to nothing, and then the next fuel. 42,000 of these phases push the bound to a number with 8.7·10146 digits, but the bottom of the tape refills its fuels as fast as they are used, so the event itself is still out of reach.

Run on from there, with three fixes to the accelerator, for 12,482 phases: the next fuel of an eater is either built fresh by the hits the phase passes down (one new rung for every 11 hits, or for every 21) or an older run of the word. Below the eater the word is a list of staircases, runs of the rung a factor of 4 apart, and this list grows: 362 long runs at wall visit 103200, 5,257 after 12,000 phases. Every one of them has to be burnt before a hit can reach the right end, so the event is not coming closer. The arithmetic of a descent (how fast the fuel shrinks, and that the bounds of the phases multiply) is proved in Lean; the laws themselves are measured, not proved.

Why this does not settle the question: the events never stop coming, each one rewrites the far end of the tape in a way that is only known by running it, and there are words on which the machine halts. Nothing so far says that such a word can never be left behind.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

explainer.title: One map on words, and a counter in base 4 inside it

family: nested base-4 counter on pairs (word recursion) with fuel, eater and right-end events
summary: Wall visits iterate a recursion on digit words (levels (10)^n in base 4, fuel (100)^m, an eater that builds new levels); an accelerator validated on 2·10^10 steps passes the seventh right-end event (wall visit 4.1·10^148) and reaches wall visit about 10^25600 (step 1.7·10^51200) without a halt; events keep coming, so the question is open.
